thread:
maya: Heads-up — dashboards spiked on P95 yesterday, looks like the auth check fanout is the culprit. Payloads are small but each panel does a full policy eval.

dmitri: saw that in tracing. auth service 99th jumped from 60ms -> 220ms for multi-tenant queries.

lina: is this primarily RBAC decision complexity or cache churn + invalidations?

dmitri: mostly complexity. Current flow is "fetch user roles -> evaluate policy per row/panel -> fetch resource metadata". No prefix pushdown so every panel repeats work.

maya: proposal: introduce a fast-path for read-only dashboard queries that uses a precomputed permission bitmap (tenant+panel level) stored in the query layer cache. If bitmap says allowed -> skip full policy engine, else fall back.

sam: nice. Tradeoffs? Staleness could allow reads after a role revocation if cache hasn't invalidated.

maya: agreed. Plan includes short TTL (15s) + immediate invalidation on role change events for affected tenants. Also attach auth-version to responses so clients can detect stale views.

lina: also consider a conservative default: fast-path only for panels with no row-level policies (materialized dashboards). We should maintain a whitelist in metadata.

dmitri: re: implementation sketch:

```
// on policy change
invalidate_cached_bitmap(tenant, panel)
publish_event("auth.invalidate", {tenant, panel, auth_version})

// query path
bitmap = cache.get(tenant, panel)
if (bitmap && bitmap.allows(user)) return fast_result
else call_full_policy_engine()
```

maya: metrics to track: fastpath_hits, fastpath_misses, stale_rejects, time_saved_ms_per_panel. SLO target: reduce dashboard p95 by 30% within canary orgs.

paul: rollout idea: feature-flag the fast-path per org. Start with internal + 3 small customers. Canary for 48h, verify no permission regressions, then 2-week ramp.

sam: what about multi-panel queries that combine different resource types? Need consistent auth_version across the whole page.

maya: we'll compute page-level auth_version = max(panel.auth_version) and if any panel is stale -> fall back to full evaluation for whole page. Simpler and safe.

lina: audit logging: log all fast-path grants for first 24h post-rollout so security can review any misses.

console-bot: deploy pipeline triggered for branch fastpath-authz (CI: unit/integ passed)

dmitri: follow-ups: (1) add invalidation hooks in KMS user-role API, (2) perf test harness for synthetic dashboards, (3) update rollout playbook with rollback steps.

maya: I'll open tracking tickets and a short RFC doc. Taking action items: write perf test, wire event invalidate, and prepare canary org list.

sam: thumbs up. minor nit: document the eventual long-term plan to move row-level policies into the data plane for truly constant-time checks (RFC phase 2).

maya: noted. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
